methods.cut: whole links (sweet or hot Italian sausage)
methods.time: 1 hour total (20 minutes covered with foil, 40 minutes uncovered to brown)
methods.doneness: Internal temperature reaches 160°F (71.1°C); casings are browned and blistered
methods.tips: Prick casings lightly with a fork to release steam and prevent casing ruptures; tossing with sliced bell peppers and onions creates a rich pan jus.

source.name: Idiot's Kitchen Recipe – Baked Italian Sausage with Peppers & Onions

methods.heat: Medium to medium-high heat in a skillet
methods.doneness: Cooked through, no pink remains, reaches 160°F internal, and browned fond forms on bottom of skillet
methods.rest: None; drain excess rendered grease if desired, then deglaze fond with wine, broth, or aromatics
methods.tips: Break meat into bite-sized clumps with a wooden spatula; let sit undisturbed for the first 2 minutes to promote rich Maillard browning rather than steaming.

source.name: Creamy Tuscan Sausage Pasta - Get Inspired Everyday! & Boston.gov

methods.cut: sliced cooked links or browned crumbles
methods.doneness: Tender, succulent texture; infused throughout broth (minimum 160°F internal)
methods.tips: Brown sausage first in the soup pot to establish fond before pouring in broth, cannellini beans, and bitter greens (escarole or kale).

avoid.warning: Violent, aggressive boiling or high-heat direct searing of raw links: high intense heat causes the fat inside the casing to rapidly expand and burst the casing, losing savory juices and causing grill flare-ups.
Under有意 cooking ground pork below the strict 160°F internal threshold; raw or rare pork sausage presents food safety hazards.
Crowding the skillet when browning bulk sausage: overcrowding lowers pan temperature and causes ground meat to boil in its own expelled liquid rather than searing and caramelizing.
